note: Hero pairs: a photograph and its line made as one idea, served outside the slot grid (Al + Maat, 14 Oct 2026). Each pair carries its own rules instead of a grid slot: its condition folder, the times of day and the SAST weekdays (Mon=1 … Sun=7) it fits. assets/image-picker.js pickHeroPair gives each pair ONE of its allowed days per week in its cell (the day moves week by week; two pairs in one cell never share a day); the library serves every other day. This file is the source: scripts/build-hero-pairs.mjs writes the picker table, scripts/build-hero-lines.mjs the English lines, scripts/build-hero-crop-offsets.mjs the crop anchors; each refuses a pair whose bytes no longer match sha1. A pair is approved rendered on the phone with its stranger-read sentence, never as text (Al + Maat, 14 Oct 2026).

lines: Clear sky this morning. Anyone driving east is doing it from memory.
pairs.af: Helder lug vanoggend. Wie oos ry, ry maar uit die kop uit.
pairs.stranger: A reader who has lost someone on the road could hear it as glib about driving blind; it stays because it names a shared nuisance, not a risk anyone takes for fun.

lines: Not a cloud all day. The only tree in the car park is now prime property.
pairs.af: Heeldag nie 'n wolkie nie. Die enigste boom op die parkeerterrein is nou prima eiendom.
pairs.stranger: It could be read as sneering at drivers who won't park in the sun; nobody in it is identifiable, and every reader is one of those drivers.

lines: Mostly sunny. Except over your garden.
pairs.af: Oorwegend sonnig. Behalwe bo jou erf.
pairs.stranger: With a South African Indian family in the frame, a stranger could read 'your garden' as aimed at them; the line speaks to the reader, and the father's flat look up at the cloud makes him the one in on the joke.

lines: It's looked like rain since breakfast. Still just looking.
pairs.af: Dit lyk al van ontbyt af na reën. Lyk is al wat dit doen.
pairs.stranger: With nobody in the frame, the line can only be about the sky.

lines: The sun didn't show for sundowners. Everyone else did.
pairs.af: Die son het nie vir sundowners opgedaag nie. Die res van ons wel.
pairs.stranger: It could be read as a dig at older people who drink no matter what; they are a mixed group of friends seen from behind, and the joke is on the sun.

lines: Steady breeze from next door's braai. You get everything but the meat.
pairs.af: Die wind waai reg van die bure se braai af. Jy kry alles behalwe die vleis.
pairs.stranger: It could be read as a joke about who can afford meat; there is no person in the frame, only a dog and a wall, and it is plainly a Saturday in a cared-for yard.

lines: A proper breeze tonight. The mosquitoes have been grounded.
pairs.af: Lekker bries vanaand. Die muskiete kan nie land nie.
pairs.stranger: A reader could see a young woman alone outside at night as a worry rather than a pleasure; she is on her own back stoep, behind a wall, with the door open and the dog asleep beside her.

lines: Good rain. Oupa's already phoning round: 'How much did you get?'
pairs.af: Goeie reën. Oupa bel al klaar rond: 'Hoeveel het julle gehad?'
pairs.stranger: Calling an old Coloured man 'Oupa' could sting if it sounded like the old diminutives; it is the word his own grandchildren use, and he is shown at his own gauge, on his own land, delighted.

lines: Raining all night. The sprinkler hasn't noticed.
pairs.af: Dit reën die hele nag. Die sprinkelaar het nog nie agtergekom nie.
pairs.stranger: In a water-scarce country it could read as a dig at people who waste water; the rain is doing the watering either way, and nobody is shown.

lines: In and out of the sun all day, then this. We all know someone like that.
pairs.af: Heeldag son-in, son-uit, en dan dít. Ons ken almal so iemand.
pairs.stranger: Someone could hear 'someone like that' as a dig at a moody partner or parent; it's warm, and it's the sky that's being described.

lines: Proper gale tonight. If you're towing a caravan, the caravan is driving.
pairs.af: Stormwind vanaand. As jy 'n karavaan sleep, bestuur die karavaan.
pairs.stranger: A reader who has lost someone on the road could hear it as making light of a dangerous drive; nobody is shown and the joke is on the wind.

lines: Proper heat this afternoon. Even the candles can't stand up straight.
pairs.af: Behoorlik warm vanmiddag. Selfs die kerse kan nie regop staan nie.
pairs.stranger: Hard to find one: there is nobody in it, and candles are only candles.

lines: Frost in the shade. The bus queue has moved into the sun.
pairs.af: Ryp in die skaduwee. Die bustou het in die son gaan staan.
pairs.stranger: A reader could see working people waiting in the cold as hardship; they are shown warm-coated, clever about it and in a neat town, and the joke is on the frost.

lines: Thick mist on the dam this morning. The fish have the same view as you.
pairs.af: Dik mis oor die dam vanoggend. Die visse het dieselfde uitsig as jy.
pairs.stranger: Hard to find one: an older man at his favourite spot, the joke is on the fish.

lines: The hadedas are heading home early. Follow them.
pairs.af: Die hadedas gaan vroeg huis toe. Gaan saam.
pairs.stranger: Hard to find one: three birds and a sky.

lines: Cold, wet and grey. The car smells of vinegar. Correct.
pairs.af: Koud, nat en grys. Die kar ruik na asyn. Presies reg.
pairs.stranger: Hard to find one: two people sharing chips in their own car, nobody's body or habits are the joke.

lines: Big wind today. The avo tree is having a clearance sale.
pairs.af: Groot wind vandag. Die avokadoboom hou uitverkoping.
pairs.stranger: A reader could see an elderly woman picking fruit off the ground as hardship; it is her own tree in her own cared-for yard, and she is delighted.
pairs.source: review/opus-ten-b/b07-wind-day-avos.r1.png (q69, softened 0.6 px to fit the budget, 295134 bytes)

lines: Thick mist this morning. The spiders have been busy all along.
pairs.af: Dik mis vanoggend. Die spinnekoppe was heeltyd besig.
pairs.stranger: Someone afraid of spiders won't love it; nobody is in the frame.

lines: Hot enough that the ref's calling a water break every ten minutes.
pairs.af: So warm, die skeidsregter blaas elke tien minute vir 'n waterpouse.
pairs.stranger: A reader could worry about children playing in dangerous heat; the picture shows the adult in charge doing the right thing.

lines: Cold and wet all day. The furniture has slowly moved closer to the heater.
pairs.af: Heeldag koud en nat. Die meubels het stadig nader aan die verwarmer geskuif.
pairs.stranger: Hard to find one: a woman warm in her own lounge, the joke is on the furniture.
